definition: a member of a people regarded as primitive or uncivilized
hook: The Greeks had a word for everyone who was not Greek. It was an impression of what they sounded like.
modernAnchor: Conquest, pillage, chaos at the gates of Rome. We picture fur, swords, and shouting.
journey: To Greek ears, all foreign tongues sounded the same: bar bar bar, meaningless noise.
The Greeks called anyone who did not speak Greek a barbaros, a babbler, a stammerer.
Romans borrowed the word and hardened it. Barbarians were not just foreign. They were lesser.
An entire civilization's contempt for outsiders compressed into two syllables, repeated twice.

payoff.revelation: SOMEONE WHO SAYS BAR BAR BAR
